Major Depressive Disorder

criteria · adequate trial · switch, augment or electroconvulsive therapy · continuation and maintenance · drug choice by comorbidityHas the drug had a fair trial, and how long should it continue?

1Frame2Act now3Differential4Workup5Confirm6Stratify7Treat8FollowPractice
1Frame

Weeks of depressed mood or lost interest, with distress or impairment.

unipolar vs bipolarprimary vs substance or medicaltoo early vs a failed trial

Bottom line
  • Five or more symptoms for 2 weeks, one of them depressed mood or loss of interest, with impairment.
  • Ask about past mania or hypomania before any antidepressant: one episode makes it bipolar, and an antidepressant alone can switch it to mania.
  • Specifiers change the first move: psychotic features, an antidepressant plus an antipsychotic or ECT; catatonia, lorazepam.
  • Judge a drug only after an adequate trial: at least 4 to 6 weeks at a therapeutic dose; partial response, raise the dose first.
  • After remission, continue about 6 more months at the same dose.
What MDD does, by systemsupports, never diagnoses
Sleep and EEGShorter REM latency; more REM early in the night; less slow-wave sleep; early-morning awakening
HPA axisHigh cortisol; no suppression after dexamethasone; high CSF CRHglucocorticoid receptor function is reduced, so cortisol fails to shut its own axis off
MonoaminesDisturbed serotonin activity; norepinephrine and dopamine also implicatedreuptake blockers and MAOIs work by raising them
Brain structureSmaller hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex; low serum BDNFchronic stress contributes to the hippocampal and prefrontal loss
ImmuneHigher IL-6, TNF-alpha and CRPcytokines may divert tryptophan from serotonin synthesis to the kynurenine pathway
Appetite and weightMelancholic: anorexia, weight loss, early waking. Atypical: mood that brightens with good news, more appetite, hypersomnia, leaden paralysis, rejection sensitivity
2Act now
High riskFrequent thoughts with a specific plan and intent to act soon, or rehearsal or preparation
Ask directly: asking does not cause or worsen it

If high risk, choose hospitalization, involuntary if refused.

Low riskNo or infrequent thoughts, no plan or intent, many protective factors
Not a no-suicide contract: it does not prevent suicide

If low risk, choose a safety plan, removal of firearms and medications, treatment and follow-up.

3Differential
Look-alikes, most tempting first
DiagnosisFingerprintDecides it
Major depressive disorder5 of 9 symptoms for 2 weeks, with impairmentNever manic or hypomanic; no cause found
must not missDepressed now, manic or hypomanic beforeAny past manic or hypomanic episode
The same symptoms with physical or laboratory abnormalities (eg, Cushing syndrome)Medical evaluation finds the cause
Persistent depressive disorderDepressed most days for 2 years or more (1 year, possibly irritable, in children and adolescents)Duration of 2 years or more
Adjustment disorderDistress out of proportion, within 3 months of a stressorFull major depressive criteria not met
Normal griefSadness after a deathFull criteria still mean major depressive disorder; bereavement does not exclude it
Psychosis plus mood episodesPsychosis for 2 weeks or more with no mood episode
4Workup
Clues that change the diagnosis
CluePoints toNext move
Past mania or hypomaniaA bipolar disorder, not MDDBipolar pathway; no antidepressant alone
Depressed most days, 2 years or morePersistent depressive disorderDuration decides the name
Full criteria after a death or stressorStill MDDTreat as MDD
Stressor within 3 months, criteria not metAdjustment disorderNot MDD

Pause point. The bait: a depressed patient who hears voices, offered as schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. Psychosis only inside the depressive episode is MDD with psychotic features: an antidepressant plus an antipsychotic, or ECT. Psychosis for 2 weeks or more with no mood episode, while mood episodes fill most of the illness, is schizoaffective disorder.

5Confirm
Defining criteria Symptoms – 5 or more of 9, most of the day, nearly every day, for at least 2 weeks; at least one is depressed mood or loss of interest · The 9 – depressed mood plus the 8 of SIGECAPS · Impairment – clinically significant distress or impairment · Exclusions – not due to a substance, a medication or a medical condition (eg, hypothyroidism); never a manic or hypomanic episode
SIGECAPS
  • Sleep – insomnia or hypersomnia
  • Interest – loss of interest or pleasure
  • Guilt – worthlessness or excessive guilt
  • Energy – fatigue, loss of energy
  • Concentration – poor concentration or indecisiveness
  • Appetite – appetite or weight change
  • Psychomotor – agitation or retardation
  • Suicide – thoughts of death or suicide

Add depressed mood for the 9 criteria; 5 or more, and one must be depressed mood or loss of interest.

Clinical diagnosis: laboratory studies only exclude medical causes
6Stratify
PHQ-9Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by:
Item0Not at all1Several days2More than half the days3Nearly every day
1Little interest or pleasure in doing things
2Feeling down, depressed or hopeless
3Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
4Feeling tired or having little energy
5Poor appetite or overeating
6Feeling bad about yourself, a failure, or letting yourself or your family down
7Trouble concentrating, eg, reading or watching television
8Moving or speaking slowly enough for others to notice, or so fidgety you move around more than usual
9Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourselfAny score above 0: suicide risk assessment, step 2

Score each item 0 to 3 and add them: total 0 to 27.

10 or morelikely major depression: sensitivity and specificity 88%
0 to 4minimalno treatment
5 to 9mildpsychotherapy first, or watchful waiting with a repeat PHQ-9
10 to 14moderatetreatment plan: counseling and/or medication; together they beat either alone
15 to 19moderately severeactive treatment: medication and/or psychotherapy
20 to 27severestart medication now; refer if impairment is severe or response is poor
Specifiers
SpecifierRecognize itChoose
Psychotic featuresDelusions or hallucinations inside the depressive episodeAn antidepressant plus an antipsychotic, or ECT
CatatoniaMutism, abnormal postures, staring, purposeless movementLorazepam first; ECT if it fails or is malignantAntipsychotics can worsen it
Peripartum onsetOnset in pregnancy or within 4 weeks after deliveryBlues: start within 2 to 3 days, gone by 2 weeks, no impairment; not a disorderPsychotherapy and/or sertraline or escitalopram; breastfeeding can continuePostpartum psychosis: an emergency
Seasonal patternFall and winter onset, spring and summer remissionLight therapy, 10,000 lux, 30 minutes daily
Atypical featuresMood brightens with good news; more appetite, hypersomnia, leaden paralysis, rejection sensitivityFirst-line drugs; an MAOI if they fail
EscalateVery severe (persistent suicidality, or refusal to eat or drink), psychotic features, or several failed drug trials

If any of these, choose ECT (electroconvulsive therapy).

7Treat
Before the first doseAny past mania or hypomania?

If yes, choose the bipolar pathway; no antidepressant alone.

1

1st linestart here

An MechanismSelective serotonin reuptake inhibitor: blocks the serotonin transporter, so more serotonin stays in the synaptic cleft; little effect on dopamine or norepinephrine. The full effect may take up to 6 weeks.Why it fits depression is linked to disturbed central serotonin activity; norepinephrine and dopamine are also implicated., SNRI (serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor), MechanismBlocks dopamine and norepinephrine transporters.Watch for no sexual dysfunction, one of very few antidepressants; it lowers the seizure threshold. or MechanismBlocks central presynaptic alpha-2 receptors, 5-HT2A, 5-HT2C and 5-HT3 receptors, and histamine H1 receptors.Watch for drowsiness, a bigger appetite and weight gain.

Similarly effective: the table below picks the drug.

Children and young adults: watch for new suicidal thoughts Pregnancy: avoid paroxetine

Under 4 to 6 weeks at a therapeutic dose: same drug, same dose

2

Raisepartly better after an adequate trial

Optimize the dose first

Go toward the maximum tolerated dose, then give it 4 to 6 weeks before adding a drug.

3

Switchminimal or no improvement after an adequate trial

A different SSRI, or a first-line drug with another mechanism

For example, an SNRI such as venlafaxine.

4

Addsevere and only partly better after 6 to 12 weeks

Psychotherapy, or a second-generation antipsychotic

Antipsychotic side effects include akathisia, sedation and weight gain. Lithium is an add-on, never monotherapy.

5

Lastseveral first-line trials have failed

A MechanismTricyclic antidepressant: blocks serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake, and also blocks muscarinic, histamine H1 and alpha-adrenergic receptors.Watch for overdose prolongs the QTc and widens the QRS. or an MechanismMonoamine oxidase inhibitor: blocks the enzyme that breaks down monoamines, so their levels rise.Watch for hypertensive reactions; serotonin syndrome when combined with other serotonergic drugs.

Poor tolerability and safety limit their use.

Before an MAOI: at least 5 weeks off fluoxetine, 2 weeks off others
First drug by situation
SituationChooseWatch for
Bulimia, anorexia or seizuresNot bupropion; in bulimia, fluoxetine (fewer binges, less vomiting)Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold
Weight gain or sexual dysfunction a concernBupropionOnly without a contraindication
Insomnia or poor appetiteMirtazapine: sedating, raises appetiteWeight gain
Older adultSertraline, escitalopram or duloxetineAvoid paroxetine and fluoxetineCheck sodium 2 to 4 weeks after starting (hyponatremia)
8Follow
under 4 wktoo early to judge
4 to 6 wkadequate trial
remissionsame dose
+6 mocontinuation (4 to 9 months)
yearsmaintenance if high risk
Follow-up decisions
WhenDo
Remission reachedSame dose for 4 to 9 more months: the dose that brought remission is the dose that holds it
Continuation done, relapse risk not highTaper over at least 2 weeks, then stop
Unstable remission, or 2 or more episodesMaintenance for 2 years or more
3 or more episodesMaintenance, often indefinite
Stopping any antidepressantTaper; paroxetine and venlafaxine cause the most discontinuation symptoms, fluoxetine the least
On any antidepressantWatch for worsening and new suicidal thoughts, most of all in children and young adults
Practice
  1. 34-year-old man, low mood 3 weeks since losing his job most days: sleeps poorly, lost interest, tired, can't focus, feels worthless stopped looking for work Never had elevated mood no drug or alcohol use · T 36.8 °C · TSH normal → Major depressive disorder → five symptoms including depressed mood and loss of interest, most days for 2 weeks or more, with impairment; no hypomania ever, so not bipolar II; a normal TSH makes a thyroid cause unlikely
  2. 26-year-old man started citalopram at a therapeutic dose 2 weeks ago a final exam is this week; mood dipped again the past 2 days Headache in week 1 resolved; no suicidal ideation HR 72/min · BP 120/74 mm Hg → Keep the current citalopram dose → 2 weeks is not an adequate trial (at least 4 to 6 weeks at a therapeutic dose); a few low days, partly from stress, do not mean failure, and a higher dose only adds adverse effects
  3. 29-year-old woman with depression on maximum-dose fluoxetine for 8 weeks minimal change in mood, energy or concentration; takes it daily Prior anorexia nervosa, now at a healthy weight; no suicidal ideation BP 112/70 mm Hg · potassium 4.1 mEq/L → Switch to venlafaxine → 8 weeks at the maximum dose is already an adequate trial, so switch to another first-line antidepressant; bupropion is contraindicated with a current or prior diagnosis of bulimia or anorexia nervosa
  4. 27-year-old woman with 6 weeks of sadness, hypersomnia and worthlessness eats large amounts in secret, then feels she must undo it hates her body BP 102/66 mm Hg · potassium 3.0 mEq/L · chloride 90 mEq/L · bicarbonate 33 mEq/L → Bupropion → low potassium and chloride point to self-induced vomiting; bupropion is contraindicated with bulimia or anorexia nervosa (seizure risk); fluoxetine can also reduce binge eating and vomiting; mirtazapine is a poor fit (appetite, drowsiness) but not contraindicated
  5. 61-year-old woman with her first depressive episode on paroxetine 20 mg; at 10 weeks every symptom has resolved tolerating it; would like to cut down or stop soon euthymic, full affect · no suicidal ideation · BP 128/80 mm Hg → Continue 20 mg for about 6 more months → continuation at the dose that achieved remission lowers relapse (6 more months: 41% to 12%); afterward, if still in remission, taper gradually
  6. 52-year-old woman in remission 6 months on escitalopram this was her third major depressive episode; each followed stopping treatment wants to know how long to stay on it euthymic · no suicidal ideation · BP 124/78 mm Hg → Continue escitalopram indefinitely → three or more episodes: indefinite maintenance is often recommended; two or more episodes already carry a high risk of relapse
  7. 67-year-old man with severe major depression for 6 weeks barely speaks, eats almost nothing, believes his organs are rotting lost 6 kg; sertraline started 3 weeks ago T 37.0 °C · HR 98/min · dry mucous membranes → Electroconvulsive therapy → psychotic depression with poor intake and weight loss needs a rapid response; both are indications for electroconvulsive therapy
Pairs with Bipolar Disorder: was there ever a manic or hypomanic episode? SSRI Adverse Effects: is the new complaint an adverse effect or discontinuation, not relapse?
Transferable rule

Check the clock before changing the plan: no switch before an adequate trial, and no stop before continuation is complete.
